from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Legend and the Rules", 
            [
                "Welcome to the legendary Towers of Hanoi puzzle.",
                "Three pegs, graduated disks, and one ultimate goal.",
                "Rule one: move only one disk at a time.",
                "Rule two: never place larger disks on smaller ones.",
                "Move the stack using the fewest moves possible."
            ]
        )
        
        # Define colors
        COLOR_PEG = "#808080"
        COLOR_DISK1 = "#FF0000" # Red (Smallest)
        COLOR_DISK2 = "#00FF00" # Green (Medium)
        COLOR_DISK3 = "#0000FF" # Blue (Largest)
        COLOR_X = "#FF0000"
        COLOR_GOLD = "#FFD700"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Create Pegs
        peg_a = Line(self.grid["B2"], self.grid["F2"], color=COLOR_PEG, stroke_width=8)
        peg_b = Line(self.grid["B4"], self.grid["F4"], color=COLOR_PEG, stroke_width=8)
        peg_c = Line(self.grid["B6"], self.grid["F6"], color=COLOR_PEG, stroke_width=8)
        
        label_a = Text("A", font_size=24).next_to(peg_a, UP, buff=0.2)
        label_b = Text("B", font_size=24).next_to(peg_b, UP, buff=0.2)
        label_c = Text("C", font_size=24).next_to(peg_c, UP, buff=0.2)
        
        # Create Disks
        disk_blue = RoundedRectangle(width=1.6, height=0.4, corner_radius=0.1, fill_color=COLOR_DISK3, fill_opacity=1, stroke_width=2)
        disk_green = RoundedRectangle(width=1.2, height=0.4, corner_radius=0.1, fill_color=COLOR_DISK2, fill_opacity=1, stroke_width=2)
        disk_red = RoundedRectangle(width=0.8, height=0.4, corner_radius=0.1, fill_color=COLOR_DISK1, fill_opacity=1, stroke_width=2)
        
        # Stack disks on Peg A (Positions: E2, D2, C2)
        self.place_at_grid(disk_blue, "E2")
        self.place_at_grid(disk_green, "D2")
        self.place_at_grid(disk_red, "C2")
        
        self.play(Create(peg_a), Create(peg_b), Create(peg_c), Write(label_a), Write(label_b), Write(label_c))
        self.play(FadeIn(disk_blue), FadeIn(disk_green), FadeIn(disk_red))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Parabolic move Red: A top (C2) to C bottom (E6)
        path = ArcBetweenPoints(start=self.grid["C2"], end=self.grid["E6"], angle=-TAU/4)
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(disk_red, path), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Move Green A -> B
        self.play(disk_green.animate.move_to(self.grid["E4"]), run_time=1)
        
        # Attempt to move Blue A -> B (Illegal: Larger on Smaller)
        target_pos = self.grid["D4"] # Position above Green disk
        midpoint = (self.grid["E2"] + target_pos) / 2 + UP * 0.5
        
        self.play(disk_blue.animate.move_to(midpoint), run_time=0.8)
        
        # Show flashing 'X'
        cross = VGroup(
            Line(midpoint + LEFT*0.3 + UP*0.3, midpoint + RIGHT*0.3 + DOWN*0.3, color=COLOR_X, stroke_width=10),
            Line(midpoint + LEFT*0.3 + DOWN*0.3, midpoint + RIGHT*0.3 + UP*0.3, color=COLOR_X, stroke_width=10)
        )
        self.play(FadeIn(cross))
        self.play(Flash(cross, color=COLOR_X, flash_radius=0.5))
        self.play(FadeOut(cross))
        
        # Return Blue to Peg A
        self.play(disk_blue.animate.move_to(self.grid["E2"]), run_time=0.8)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Transition to target state on Peg C
        target_blue = disk_blue.copy().move_to(self.grid["E6"])
        target_green = disk_green.copy().move_to(self.grid["D6"])
        target_red = disk_red.copy().move_to(self.grid["C6"])
        
        target_stack = VGroup(target_blue, target_green, target_red)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(disk_red),
            FadeOut(disk_green),
            FadeOut(disk_blue),
            FadeIn(target_stack)
        )
        
        # Gold Glow effect
        glow = target_stack.copy().set_color(COLOR_GOLD).set_opacity(0.3).scale(1.1)
        self.play(
            target_stack.animate.set_stroke(COLOR_GOLD, 4),
            FadeIn(glow),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=2
        )
        self.play(FadeOut(glow))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines
        lecture_lines = [
            "Let's look at the pulse of binary counting.",
            "We count from zero up to seven for three disks.",
            "Each increment flips at least one bit.",
            "Focus on the rightmost bit that changes state.",
            "This flipping bit is the key to our puzzle."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: Binary Counting as a Pulse", lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = "#FFFF00"  # Yellow
        NORMAL_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"     # White

        # Prepare binary number list (000 to 111)
        # Each number is a VGroup of 3 digits
        binary_list = VGroup(*[
            VGroup(*[Text(char, font_size=36, color=NORMAL_COLOR) for char in bin(i)[2:].zfill(3)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
            for i in range(8)
        ]).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
        
        # Position the list in the middle-right area
        self.place_in_area(binary_list, "A3", "F4", scale_factor=1.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Let's look at the pulse of binary counting.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # We count from zero up to seven for three disks.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(NORMAL_COLOR),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        )
        self.play(Create(binary_list), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Each increment flips at least one bit.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(NORMAL_COLOR),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Highlight transition from 000 (binary_list[0]) to 001 (binary_list[1])
        # The last bit of 001 flips (0 -> 1)
        rect1 = SurroundingRectangle(binary_list[1][2], color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(rect1))
        self.play(binary_list[1][2].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Focus on the rightmost bit that changes state.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(NORMAL_COLOR),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Transition from 001 (binary_list[1]) to 010 (binary_list[2])
        # Prompt: highlighting the second bit as the rightmost change.
        rect2 = SurroundingRectangle(binary_list[2][1], color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR, buff=0.1)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(rect1, rect2))
        self.play(binary_list[2][1].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # This flipping bit is the key to our puzzle.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(NORMAL_COLOR),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Final visual: show how the "pulse" continues down the list
        # Highlight the "rightmost flipping bit" for the rest of the list
        # 011: bit 3; 100: bit 1; 101: bit 3; 110: bit 2; 111: bit 3
        highlights = [
            (3, 2), # Row 3 (011), Bit index 2
            (4, 0), # Row 4 (100), Bit index 0
            (5, 2), # Row 5 (101), Bit index 2
            (6, 1), # Row 6 (110), Bit index 1
            (7, 2)  # Row 7 (111), Bit index 2
        ]
        
        pulse_anims = []
        for row_idx, bit_idx in highlights:
            pulse_anims.append(binary_list[row_idx][bit_idx].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR))
            
        self.play(FadeOut(rect2))
        self.play(*pulse_anims, run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize Scene
        lecture_lines = [
            "Every bit corresponds to a specific disk size.",
            "The rightmost changing bit identifies the moving disk.",
            "Binary 001 moves disk one; 010 moves disk two."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Perfect Mapping", lecture_lines)

        # Color definitions
        COLOR_D1 = "#00FFFF" # Cyan
        COLOR_D2 = "#FF00FF" # Magenta
        COLOR_D3 = "#FFFFFF" # White

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight first line
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))

        # Create Disk Representations
        d3 = RoundedRectangle(width=2.5, height=0.5, color=COLOR_D3, fill_opacity=0.3)
        d2 = RoundedRectangle(width=1.8, height=0.5, color=COLOR_D3, fill_opacity=0.3)
        d1 = RoundedRectangle(width=1.1, height=0.5, color=COLOR_D3, fill_opacity=0.3)

        self.place_at_grid(d3, "C2")
        self.place_at_grid(d2, "C3")
        self.place_at_grid(d1, "C4")

        # Labels
        label3 = Text("Disk 3", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        label2 = Text("Disk 2", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        label1 = Text("Disk 1", font_size=20, color=WHITE)

        self.place_at_grid(label3, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(label2, "B3")
        self.place_at_grid(label1, "B4")

        # Binary Bits
        bit3 = Text("0", font_size=40, color=WHITE)
        bit2 = Text("0", font_size=40, color=WHITE)
        bit1 = Text("0", font_size=40, color=WHITE)

        self.place_at_grid(bit3, "D2")
        self.place_at_grid(bit2, "D3")
        self.place_at_grid(bit1, "D4")

        self.play(
            FadeIn(d1), FadeIn(d2), FadeIn(d3),
            Write(label1), Write(label2), Write(label3)
        )
        self.play(Write(bit1), Write(bit2), Write(bit3))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )

        # Show transition 000 -> 001
        new_bit1_1 = Text("1", font_size=40, color=COLOR_D1).move_to(bit1)
        
        self.play(
            Transform(bit1, new_bit1_1),
            Indicate(new_bit1_1, color=COLOR_D1, scale_factor=1.5),
            d1.animate.set_fill(COLOR_D1, opacity=0.8)
        )
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(d1.animate.set_fill(COLOR_D3, opacity=0.3))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_D2)
        )

        # Show transition 001 -> 010
        # Rightmost CHANGING bit is what we focus on (Bit 2 in this case for the step)
        new_bit1_0 = Text("0", font_size=40, color=WHITE).move_to(bit1)
        new_bit2_1 = Text("1", font_size=40, color=COLOR_D2).move_to(bit2)

        self.play(
            Transform(bit1, new_bit1_0),
            Transform(bit2, new_bit2_1),
            Indicate(new_bit2_1, color=COLOR_D2, scale_factor=1.5),
            d2.animate.set_fill(COLOR_D2, opacity=0.8)
        )
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(d2.animate.set_fill(COLOR_D3, opacity=0.3))

        # Show transition 010 -> 011
        new_bit1_1_v2 = Text("1", font_size=40, color=COLOR_D1).move_to(bit1)

        self.play(
            Transform(bit1, new_bit1_1_v2),
            Indicate(new_bit1_1_v2, color=COLOR_D1, scale_factor=1.5),
            d1.animate.set_fill(COLOR_D1, opacity=0.8)
        )
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(d1.animate.set_fill(COLOR_D3, opacity=0.3))

        # Final Summary text
        summary_text = Text("Rightmost bit flip = Moving Disk", color=WHITE, font_size=26)
        self.place_in_area(summary_text, "E1", "F6")
        self.play(Write(summary_text))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data
        title = "The Directional Logic"
        lines = [
            "Disk one always follows a specific cyclic direction.",
            "Other disks move to the only legal open spot.",
            "This creates a rhythmic, predictable pattern of movement."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_1 = "#FFFF00" # Yellow
        COLOR_2 = "#00FFFF" # Cyan
        COLOR_3 = "#00FF00" # Green

        # Objects Setup
        # Pegs in triangle
        peg_a = Line(DOWN*0.5, UP*0.5, color=GREY_B)
        peg_b = Line(DOWN*0.5, UP*0.5, color=GREY_B)
        peg_c = Line(DOWN*0.5, UP*0.5, color=GREY_B)
        
        self.place_at_grid(peg_a, "B3")
        self.place_at_grid(peg_b, "E1")
        self.place_at_grid(peg_c, "E5")
        
        label_a = Text("Peg A", font_size=18).next_to(peg_a, UP, buff=0.1)
        label_b = Text("Peg B", font_size=18).next_to(peg_b, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        label_c = Text("Peg C", font_size=18).next_to(peg_c, DOWN, buff=0.1)

        # Arrows
        arrow_ac = CurvedArrow(self.grid["B4"], self.grid["D5"], angle=-TAU/6, color=WHITE)
        arrow_cb = CurvedArrow(self.grid["E4"], self.grid["E2"], angle=-TAU/6, color=WHITE)
        arrow_ba = CurvedArrow(self.grid["D1"], self.grid["B2"], angle=-TAU/6, color=WHITE)

        # Disk 1
        disk1 = Rectangle(width=0.4, height=0.2, fill_opacity=1, color=COLOR_1)
        disk1.move_to(peg_a.get_bottom() + UP*0.1)

        # Disk 2 (for logic illustration)
        disk2 = Rectangle(width=0.6, height=0.2, fill_opacity=1, color=COLOR_2)
        disk2.move_to(peg_a.get_bottom() + UP*0.3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_1))
        self.play(
            Create(peg_a), Create(peg_b), Create(peg_c),
            Write(label_a), Write(label_b), Write(label_c)
        )
        self.play(Create(arrow_ac), Create(arrow_cb), Create(arrow_ba))
        self.play(FadeIn(disk1))
        
        # A -> C
        self.play(disk1.animate.move_to(peg_c.get_bottom() + UP*0.1))
        self.wait(0.5)
        # C -> B
        self.play(disk1.animate.move_to(peg_b.get_bottom() + UP*0.1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_2))
        
        # Scenario: Disk 1 is at B. Show Disk 2 at A.
        self.play(FadeIn(disk2))
        
        # Destination Peg is C (A cannot move to B because Disk 1 is smaller)
        flash_rect = Square(color=COLOR_2).scale(0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(flash_rect, "E5")
        
        self.play(Indicate(peg_c, color=COLOR_2), Flash(self.grid["E5"], color=COLOR_2))
        self.play(disk2.animate.move_to(peg_c.get_bottom() + UP*0.1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_3))
        
        # Show sequence: Disk 1 move, then Legal move
        # Disk 1 moves B -> A

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines
        lecture_lines = [
            "Watch the binary counter dictate every single move.",
            "Three disks require exactly seven synchronized steps.",
            "001 flips bit one; move disk one clockwise.",
            "010 flips bit two; move disk two legally.",
            "The binary sequence completes the tower perfectly."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Execution: The 3-Disk Walkthrough", lecture_lines)

        # Helper to create disks
        def create_disk(label, width, color):
            rect = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, width=width, height=0.4, 
                                   fill_opacity=1.0, fill_color=color, stroke_color=WHITE)
            text = Text(label, font_size=20, color=BLACK)
            return VGroup(rect, text)

        # Helper to get disk position on a peg
        def get_disk_pos(peg_idx, stack_height):
            # peg_idx: 0, 1, 2 -> columns 2, 4, 6
            # stack_height: 0, 1, 2 -> rows E, D, C
            col_map = ["2", "4", "6"]
            row_map = ["E", "D", "C"]
            return self.grid[f"{row_map[stack_height]}{col_map[peg_idx]}"]

        # === INITIAL SETUP ===
        # Create Pegs
        pegs = VGroup()
        for col in ["2", "4", "6"]:
            base = Line(self.grid[f"F{col}"] + LEFT*0.6, self.grid[f"F{col}"] + RIGHT*0.6, color=GRAY)
            rod = Line(self.grid[f"F{col}"], self.grid[f"B{col}"], color=GRAY)
            pegs.add(VGroup(base, rod))
        
        peg_labels = VGroup(
            Text("A", font_size=24).next_to(pegs[0], DOWN, buff=0.2),
            Text("B", font_size=24).next_to(pegs[1], DOWN, buff=0.2),
            Text("C", font_size=24).next_to(pegs[2], DOWN, buff=0.2)
        )
        
        # Create Disks
        d3 = create_disk("D3", 1.4, BLUE_D)
        d2 = create_disk("D2", 1.0, GREEN_D)
        d1 = create_disk("D1", 0.6, RED_D)
        disks = [d1, d2, d3] # smallest to largest
        
        # Initial positions on Peg A (idx 0)
        d3.move_to(get_disk_pos(0, 0))
        d2.move_to(get_disk_pos(0, 1))
        d1.move_to(get_disk_pos(0, 2))
        
        # Binary Counter
        counter_label = Text("Binary Step:", font_size=20, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(counter_label, "A1", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        counter_val = Text("000", font_size=36, font="Courier", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(counter_val, "A2", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        stacks = [[d3, d2, d1], [], []]

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Watch the binary counter dictate every single move."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(pegs), Write(peg_labels), FadeIn(d1, d2, d3), FadeIn(counter_label, counter_val))
        self.wait(1)

        # Helper for updating counter
        def update_counter(val_str):
            new_val = Text(val_str, font_size=36, font="Courier", color=WHITE)
            new_val.move_to(counter_val.get_center())
            return Transform(counter_val, new_val)

        # Helper for moving disk
        def move_disk_anim(disk_idx, from_peg, to_peg):
            # disk_idx: 0 for d1, 1 for d2, 2 for d3
            disk = disks[disk_idx]
            stacks[from_peg].remove(disk)
            target_pos = get_disk_pos(to_peg, len(stacks[to_peg]))
            stacks[to_peg].append(disk)
            return disk.animate.move_to(target_pos)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Three disks require exactly seven synchronized steps."
        # Animation: Execute Moves 1-3
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Step 1: 001 (D1 to C)
        self.play(update_counter("001"), move_disk_anim(0, 0, 2), run_time=0.8)
        self.wait(0.2)
        # Step 2: 010 (D2 to B)
        self.play(update_counter("010"), move_disk_anim(1, 0, 1), run_time=0.8)
        self.wait(0.2)
        # Step 3: 011 (D1 to B)
        self.play(update_counter("011"), move_disk_anim(0, 2, 1), run_time=0.8)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "001 flips bit one; move disk one clockwise."
        # Animation: Execute Move 4: 100 (Bit 3 flips, D3 moves from A to C)
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        # Step 4: 100 (D3 to C)
        self.play(update_counter("100"), move_disk_anim(2, 0, 2), run_time=1.0)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "010 flips bit two; move disk two legally."
        # Animation: Execute Moves 5-7
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        # Step 5: 101 (D1 to A)
        self.play(update_counter("101"), move_disk_anim(0, 1, 0), run_time=0.8)
        self.wait(0.2)
        # Step 6: 110 (D2 to C)
        self.play(update_counter("110"), move_disk_anim(1, 1, 2), run_time=0.8)
        self.wait(0.2)
        # Step 7: 111 (D1 to C)
        self.play(update_counter("111"), move_disk_anim(0, 0, 2), run_time=0.8)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "The binary sequence completes the tower perfectly."
        # Animation: Flash text '2^3 - 1 = 7 Moves' in green (#00FF00)
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        flash_text = Text("2^3 - 1 = 7 Moves", font_size=32, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(flash_text, "A5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(flash_text))
        self.play(Indicate(flash_text, color="#00FF00", scale_factor=1.2))
        self.wait(2)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout with title and lecture lines
        lecture_lines = [
            "Complex recursion simplifies into basic binary patterns.",
            "This logic scales from three disks to sixty-four.",
            "Mathematical beauty found in the rhythm of bits."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: The Power of Patterns", lecture_lines)

        # Colors for lines
        colors = [BLUE_C, GREEN_C, YELLOW_C]

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(colors[0]))
        
        # Create a simple 3-disk stack
        base_3 = Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color=GREY).scale(1.5)
        disks_3 = VGroup(*[
            Rectangle(width=1.5 - i*0.3, height=0.2, fill_opacity=1, color=BLUE_B, stroke_width=1)
            for i in range(3)
        ]).arrange(UP, buff=0.05).next_to(base_3, UP, buff=0)
        stack_3 = VGroup(base_3, disks_3)
        self.place_in_area(stack_3, "B2", "D4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(stack_3))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Scale down 3-disk stack and replace with 10-disk stack
        base_10 = Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color=GREY).scale(1.5)
        disks_10 = VGroup(*[
            Rectangle(width=1.8 - i*0.15, height=0.1, fill_opacity=1, color=BLUE_E, stroke_width=0.5)
            for i in range(10)
        ]).arrange(UP, buff=0.02).next_to(base_10, UP, buff=0)
        stack_10 = VGroup(base_10, disks_10)
        self.place_in_area(stack_10, "B1", "E3", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(
            stack_3.animate.scale(0.5).move_to(stack_10.get_center()),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(stack_3, stack_10))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(colors[1]))
        
        # Binary counter scrolling rapidly
        counter_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        def get_binary_text():
            val = int(counter_tracker.get_value())
            # Show binary representation with 10 bits
            bin_str = format(val, '010b')
            return Text(bin_str, font="Monospace", font_size=36, color=GREEN_B)

        binary_display = always_redraw(get_binary_text)
        self.place_at_grid(binary_display, "C5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        counter_label = Text("Steps (Binary):", font_size=20).next_to(binary_display, UP)
        self.add(counter_label)
        self.play(FadeIn(binary_display))
        
        # Scroll rapidly from 0 to 1023
        self.play(counter_tracker.animate.set_value(1023), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(colors[2]))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Fade everything out
        self.play(
            FadeOut(stack_10),
            FadeOut(binary_display),
            FadeOut(counter_label),
            FadeOut(self.title),
            FadeOut(self.lecture)
        )
        
        # Final Title
        final_title = Text("The Binary Rhythm: Pattern in Chaos", font_size=40, color=WHITE, weight=BOLD)
        # Center in the whole grid area
        self.place_in_area(final_title, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(final_title))
        self.play(Indicate(final_title, color=BLUE_A))
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: The Binary Rhythm of Hanoi: Cracking the Puzzle with 0s and 1s
outline.target_audience: High school students and introductory Computer Science students

sections.title: The Legend and the Rules
sections.content: Introduce the Towers of Hanoi puzzle: three pegs and 'n' graduated disks. Explain the two cardinal rules: move only one disk at a time, and never place a larger disk onto a smaller one. Set the goal: move the entire stack to a different peg in the minimum number of moves.
sections.example: A curious squirrel named 'Byte' stands before 3 golden pegs. He needs to move a stack of 3 disks (Red, Green, Blue) from the left peg to the right peg without breaking the 'smaller-on-top' rule.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Binary Counting as a Pulse
sections.content: Briefly review binary counting from 0 to 2^n - 1. Visualize binary numbers incrementing (000, 001, 010, 011...). Focus on the 'rightmost flipping bit'—every time we add 1, a specific bit is the first to change from 0 to 1 or 1 to 0.
sections.example: A digital ticker-tape displays binary numbers. Highlight the change: 000 → 00[1] (1st bit changes), 00[1] → 0[1]0 (2nd bit changes), 01[0] → 01[1] (1st bit changes again).

sections.title: The Perfect Mapping
sections.content: Connect binary bits to specific disks. In an n-disk puzzle, Disk 1 (smallest) corresponds to the 1st bit, Disk 2 to the 2nd bit, and so on. The rule is simple: when you increment your binary counter, the position of the rightmost bit that changed tells you exactly which disk to move.
sections.example: A graphical overlay shows Disk 1 glowing when the binary counter's last digit changes, and Disk 3 glowing only when the 4th increment (100) occurs.

sections.title: The Directional Logic
sections.content: Introduce the 'Cyclic Move' rule to determine 'where' the disk goes. For an odd number of disks: move Disk 1 in the sequence Peg A → C → B. For all other disks, move them in the remaining valid spot. This creates a predictable rhythm: Smallest disk, then a legal move not involving the smallest disk, repeat.
sections.example: Visualize Pegs A, B, and C in a circle. For Disk 1, show a clockwise arrow. For the binary count 001 (Move Disk 1), 010 (Move Disk 2), 011 (Move Disk 1), the direction follows the 'Clockwise' rule for the smallest piece.

sections.title: Execution: The 3-Disk Walkthrough
sections.content: Synthesize the binary counter and the physical moves in real-time. Show that the total moves required is exactly 2^n - 1. For 3 disks, this is 2^3 - 1 = 7 moves. Watch as the binary increments from 1 to 7, dictating every single step of the solution perfectly.
sections.example: A split-screen animation: Left side shows a binary clock ticking (001 to 111). Right side shows Byte the Squirrel moving the corresponding disks. The movement looks like a synchronized dance where the binary code is the sheet music.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Power of Patterns
sections.content: Summarize how binary counting reveals the inherent structure of recursive problems. Emphasize that what looks like a complex puzzle is actually a simple sequence of bit flips. Mention that this mapping works for any number of disks, even the legendary 64-disk version.
sections.example: The camera zooms out to show 64 disks. A fast-forward binary counter reveals that even though it would take trillions of years to finish, the 'Binary Rhythm' remains the same simple pattern.

storyboard.title: The Legend and the Rules
lecture_lines: Meet the legendary puzzle: three pegs and graduated disks.
Move the smallest disk from the left to right.
Then, move the medium disk to the middle peg.
Important: never place a larger disk onto smaller ones.
The goal: rebuild the stack on a different peg.
animations: Create three vertical gray (#808080) pegs labeled A, B, and C with 3 disks (Red #FF0000, Green #00FF00, Blue #0000FF) stacked on Peg A.
Animate the smallest Red disk moving from Peg A to Peg C in a smooth parabolic arc.
Animate the medium Green disk moving from Peg A to Peg B.
Move the largest Blue disk halfway to Peg B, show a flashing Red 'X' (#FF0000) over it, and return it to Peg A.
Highlight the target state: all 3 disks stacked on Peg C with a gold glow (#FFD700).

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: Binary Counting as a Pulse
lecture_lines: Binary numbers count the steps of our puzzle solution.
At step one, the rightmost bit flips to one.
At step two, the second bit is the rightmost flip.
animations: Display a vertical list of binary numbers from 000 to 111 in white (#FFFFFF), accompanied by the [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/steps.svg] icon to represent the sequential progression.
Transition from 000 to 001, highlighting the last bit in yellow (#FFFF00) as it flips.

Transition from 001 to 010, highlighting the second bit in yellow (#FFFF00) as the rightmost change, incorporating the [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/puzzle.svg] icon to illustrate the logical pattern.

storyboard.title: The Perfect Mapping
lecture_lines: Each disk size corresponds to a specific binary bit.
Bit one flips, so we move the smallest disk.
Now bit two flips, signaling the second disk moves.
Bit one flips again, returning focus to disk one.
The rightmost flipping bit always identifies the moving disk.
animations: Display labels 'Disk 1', 'Disk 2', and 'Disk 3' using [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/disk.svg] icons with a 3-bit binary counter '000' below.
Counter hits 001: Pulse the first bit and make the Disk 1 [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/disk.svg] glow Cyan (#00FFFF).
Counter hits 010: Pulse the second bit and make the Disk 2 [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/disk.svg] glow Magenta (#FF00FF).
Counter hits 011: Pulse the first bit again and make the Disk 1 [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/disk.svg] glow Cyan (#00FFFF).
Display text 'Rightmost bit flip = Moving Disk' in white (#FFFFFF) across the center.

storyboard.title: The Directional Logic
lecture_lines: Imagine the pegs arranged in a clockwise circle.
Disk one always follows this strict clockwise path.
Other disks simply move to the only legal spot.
animations: Position Pegs [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/peg.svg] A, B, and C in a triangle with clockwise arrows connecting them.
Show Disk [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/disk.svg] 1 (the smallest) moving from A to C, then C to B, following the clockwise sequence.
Highlight the 'only other legal move' for any non-Disk 1 piece by flashing the destination peg [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/peg.svg].

storyboard.title: Execution: The 3-Disk Walkthrough
lecture_lines: Let's synchronize the binary counter with the physical moves.
Moves one through three follow the binary rhythm perfectly.
At move four, the largest disk finally shifts position.
The final three moves complete the secondary stack.
Seven moves later, the binary sequence solves the puzzle.
animations: Split screen: Binary counter (001 to 111) on left, 3-peg Hanoi on right.
Execute Moves 1-3: 001 (D1 to C), 010 (D2 to B), 011 (D1 to B).
Execute Move 4: 100 (Bit 3 flips, D3 moves from A to C).
Execute Moves 5-7: 101 (D1 to A), 110 (D2 to C), 111 (D1 to C).
Flash text '2^3 - 1 = 7 Moves' in green (#00FF00) as the counter hits 111.

storyboard.title: Conclusion: The Power of Patterns
lecture_lines: This binary pattern scales to any number of disks.
Even complex towers follow the same simple bit flips.
Witness the mathematical beauty in this rhythmic solution.
animations: Scale down the 3-disk stack and replace it with a 10-disk stack.
Show a binary counter rapidly scrolling from 0 to 1023 next to the large stack.
Fade everything out to the title: 'The Binary Rhythm: Pattern in Chaos' in bold white (#FFFFFF).
